narrative.overview:
Burdens SOF is a logistics operations interface — the digital equivalent of a well-run dispatch floor. Everything is visible. Nothing requires interpretation. The interface has one job: put order status in front of the right person, immediately, with zero ambiguity. The design recedes so the data comes forward.

The system uses a single navigational anchor — Cobalt Ink — against a pure white ground. This is the color of precision instruments, of maritime charts, of something that works. There are no decorative layers. The hierarchy is enforced through weight, spacing, and the deliberate withholding of color until it means something: cobalt for actions, semantic green/red/amber for status, silence everywhere else.

The surface is information-dense but not cluttered. Rows breathe with consistent padding. The header is a control bar, not a billboard. Forms are austere and correct. The system should feel like it was engineered, not assembled — like it comes from a company that takes fulfilment seriously.
keyCharacteristics: Pure white ground, cobalt-only primary — one decisive accent, no noise
Status is always text-labeled; color reinforces, never substitutes
Firm, announced interactive elements — buttons and links declare themselves
Geist Sans at every scale; Geist Mono for order IDs, timestamps, and reference numbers
Subtle ambient elevation — cards breathe without drama
WCAG AA throughout — 4.5:1 for all text, 3:1 for interactive borders and UI components

rules.name: The One Anchor Rule
rules.body: Cobalt Ink is the only saturated color on any non-status surface. If a new component is reaching for a second brand hue, stop. The discipline is the design.

rules.name: The Status Text Rule
rules.body: Every status badge must carry a text label alongside its color. Color blindness is real; 'green' cannot be the only signal that an order fulfilled.

rules.name: The Muted Floor Rule
rules.body: Signal Gray (oklch(0.440)) is the lightest any secondary text may go. Anything lighter fails WCAG AA and reads as disabled.

rules.name: The Mono Discipline Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only for reference numbers, order names, and timestamps — values where fixed-width glyph alignment aids scanning. Do not use it for labels, descriptions, or UI copy.

rules.name: The Size Floor Rule
rules.body: 11px (Label scale) is the minimum text size in the interface. Warehouse staff may view this on low-resolution monitors under industrial lighting.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Every surface starts flat. A shadow is added only when the surface permanently holds scrollable or interactive content. A row, a badge, a pagination link: no shadow.

rules.name: The Shadow-Over-Both Rule
rules.body: Never apply both a shadow and a non-decorative border to the same container. Cards use shadow-card with a decorative border. Modals use shadow only.

dos: Do use Cobalt Ink (oklch(0.478 0.136 252)) as the primary action color, and only that.
Do always pair status badges with a text label — never rely on color alone.
Do use Geist Mono for order IDs, reference numbers, and timestamps.
Do keep table cell padding at 12px vertical / 16px horizontal minimum.
Do meet WCAG AA — ≥4.5:1 for all text, ≥3:1 for interactive borders and non-text UI components.
Do set font-family: var(--font-geist-sans), system-ui, sans-serif on :root in globals.css.
Do set text-wrap: balance on h1–h3 headings.
Do include prefers-reduced-motion alternatives for any transitions.
donts: Don't use cream, warm-neutral, or sand-beige page backgrounds. Background is pure white.
Don't add gradient text (background-clip: text). Prohibited.
Don't add glassmorphism or backdrop-filter blur as decoration.
Don't add a second brand color for variety. Solve flatness with spacing or weight, not hue.
Don't use side-stripe patterns (border-left > 1px as colored accent on cards or callouts).
Don't add numbered section markers (01/02/03) to navigation or page sections.
Don't add uppercase eyebrow kickers above page section headings.
Don't use light gray as body text for elegance — any text users need to read must be Control Black or Signal Gray.
Don't build icon-grid cards as the primary content pattern. This is a table interface.
Don't stack shadows — one shadow level per element.
